title: Copy a door casing's profile with a contour gauge and lay it on the vinyl to mark the cut
instruction: Copy the door casing's profile at the floor with the contour gauge, then lay the gauge flat on the vinyl sheet with the copied fingertips where the sheet must be cut to fit around the casing, and take both hands away.
context: Floor layers cut flooring to fit around obstructions (O*NET Core task) and carpenters mark cutting lines with marking gauges (Core task, 889,700 employed); a contour gauge's listing names fitting tile or linoleum around door casings as its use.
setup: Bench top = floor. Fixed: a wall block (120 mm deep, 70 mm tall) with its face 400 mm in front of the arm bases; on it a pine door casing made from 1x3 stock (19.1 x 63.5 mm, 70 mm tall) with a 6.4 x 6.4 mm rabbet on its doorway edge and a 15.9 mm wide, 9.5 mm deep rabbet on its wall edge, its doorway edge 60.5 mm right of the centre line, open floor (the doorway) to its right. Loose: a 10 in plastic contour gauge (252 mm frame, 20 x 12 mm, two 30 mm end blocks, 42 fingers 76 mm long with 31.8 mm travel, about 100 g) lying flat with its fingers set straight, frame centre 290 mm in front of the bases on the centre line, fingertips toward the casing; a 3.2 mm vinyl sheet 135 x 170 mm (120 g) on the floor nearer the arms, slid 160 mm straight back from its place, its doorway edge in line with the casing's doorway edge, a 12 mm (1/2 in) strip of masking tape across it whose near edge is the wall line, 240 mm in front of the bases.
scoring: Judged at the end. 0 unless the fingers hold a copy: over the casing and 20 mm of wall past it every finger is pushed at least 1 mm and the pushes match the casing outline within 3 mm at every finger (best place along the gauge, straight-line fit, up to 5 deg turn). 0.25: a copy. 0.5: also lying flat and still on the sheet (within 3 deg of level, frame bottom within 2 mm over the sheet top, centre over the sheet, under 0.02 m/s). 0.75: also every fingertip on the sheet (tip centres 2.5 mm inside its side edges, at least 26 fingers) within 6 mm, measured on the sheet, of the cut line with its steps drawn in: the tape's near edge over bare wall, set back by the casing outline (12.7, 19.1, 9.6 mm) over the 63.5 mm from the doorway edge. 1.0: every such fingertip within 3 mm, and both hands at least 20 mm from the gauge. Real trial: steel rule and a photo from above.
fidelity: Gauge fingers are 42 prismatic joints at 6 mm pitch (the real pins are finer), each held by a spring whose target follows it past 0.15 N (estimated finger force, to be measured with a spring scale), so a finger stays where it is pushed. The wall and casing are a 70 mm mock-up because the YAM's forearm reaches past the wall face at the copy. The pencil trace is not modelled; the task ends with the gauge set in place to trace. Frictions and masses are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (1,200 steps); demo: 1.0 (success at 32.55 s, step 651)
reset_notes: Set the gauge's fingers straight by pressing them against a flat board before each trial.
